scope: Direct children of the RedCap repository root that carry product, runtime, knowledge, evidence, policy, host-adapter, or local-state meaning.

summary.problem: RedCap's root currently exposes several directories with overlapping knowledge, report, evidence, runtime, policy, and host-adapter meanings. The system is governable, but the product shape is too hard to understand before public CLI/runtime release.
summary.solution: Freeze the current physical root as compatibility reality, define a target parent model, list consumers and risks, and require a separate apply tranche before any directory move.
summary.effect: Future cleanup has a safe map. New users and future Agents can tell which root items are public contract, internal source, private archive, local-only state, or compatibility shims.

future_apply_gate.rollback_rule: Every move must either leave a root compatibility shim or have a tested alias resolver and rollback-only cleanup path.
future_apply_gate.batching_rule: Apply at most one semantic parent group per physical migration tranche.

must_not_claim: Do not claim root directories have been physically consolidated.
Do not claim this plan makes RedCap public release ready by itself.
Do not collapse active knowledge, private cold archive, public templates, and raw evidence into one undifferentiated knowledge folder.
Do not remove host entry root files while host discovery still depends on them.
Do not publish this internal plan as part of the public runtime surface.
